## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 26 (titled *Gaṇacīvara*) governs the offense incurred by a nun who prevents an order or group of nuns from receiving a distribution of robe-cloth. In the traditional origin narrative, the nun Thullanandā creates an obstacle to the bestowal of robe material intended for a group of nuns (*gaṇassa cīvaralābhaṃ antarāyaṃ kari*), leading to complaints from the community [Hüsken 1997]. The text's legal analysis (*padabhājaniya*) clarifies that intentionally hindering robe-cloth meant for the community constitutes a pācittiya; conversely, preventing the receipt of other monastic requisites, or obstructing gifts directed to a subset of nuns, a single nun, or an unordained female, incurs only an offense of wrong conduct (*dukkaṭa*) [Hüsken 1997].

Within the Pali Vinaya, the rule is reiterated in the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and the Bhikkhunī Parivāra. External parallels are preserved in Chinese translations of the Dharmaguptaka Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga and Prātimokṣa (Pācittiya 105) and the Sarvāstivāda Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga and Prātimokṣa (Pācittiya 134). DharmaNexus additionally aligns segments of the rule with a Sanskrit Prātimokṣasūtra [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus records phraseological reuse across 85 texts, sharing its most extensive formulaic parallels with other Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga training rules, such as Pācittiya 53, Pācittiya 23, Pācittiya 27, and Pācittiya 29 [DharmaNexus].
